blocks.text: Rappler editor-at-large Marites Vitug speaks to former PAOCC officials Winnie Quidato and Winston Casio about their book, The Rogue Compound: POGOs, Human Trafficking, and the Fight to Reclaim the Philippines
Bookmark this page to catch the discussion on Friday, September 18, at 6 pm!

MANILA, Philippines – Scam compounds linked to Philippine offshore gaming operators (POGOs) have become a major organized crime problem in the country, with human trafficking, online scams, and other criminal activities converging in the same operations.

Former Presidential Anti-Organized Crime Commission (PAOCC) officials Winnie Quidato and Winston Casio draw on their experience dismantling scam compounds in their new book, The Rogue Compound: POGOs, Human Trafficking, and the Fight to Reclaim the Philippines.

On Friday, September 18, Rappler editor-at-large Marites Vitug speaks to Quidato and Casio about how scam compounds took root in the Philippines, the challenges law enforcement faced in going after them, and what it takes to dismantle these criminal networks.

Quidato is a retired police officer with decades of experience in intelligence work. He spent three years working to dismantle scam compounds as PAOCC deputy executive director. Casio, meanwhile, is a crime analyst and educator who served as PAOCC spokesperson.
With the Anti-POGO Act now in place, do POGOs still operate underground?

articles.title: UK to answer for its ‘dismal record’ in Eurovision before committee of MPs
articles.summary:
Digital, culture, media and sport committee expected to hear evidence from BBC chiefs and music industry experts

Joe and Jake. Daz Sampson. Electro Velvet. Who could forget them?

Most…

blocks.text: Joe and Jake. Daz Sampson. Electro Velvet. Who could forget them?

Most people, probably. They are among some of the many acts who represented the UK at the Eurovision song contest in the last 20 years that have failed to find a place in the country’s cultural pantheon.
Now, the chair of an influential parliamentary committee has decided to interrogate exactly why the UK has been performing so poorly.

Dame Caroline Dinenage, who heads the digital, culture, media and sport committee, told the BBC: “We want to get to the bottom of who chooses our entrant, on what basis and whether our dismal record of achievement in recent years is the result of bad song choice, weak performance … or something else.”
Prior to 2000, the UK could be proud of its efforts: it finished in the top 10 every year except in 1978, 1987 and 1999, and won with Love Shine a Light by Katrina and the Waves in 1997.

blocks.caption: Katrina and the Waves after winning Eurovision  in Dublin in May 1997.  Photograph: John Giles/AP

blocks.text: But since then it has only reached the top 10 three times and finished in last place six times – in 2003, 2008, 2010, 2019, 2021 and 2026 – with Jemini and James Newman scoring nul points in 2003 and 2021 respectively. The exception was Sam Ryder’s Space Man in 2022, which came second.
The act that represents the UK is selected by the BBC with support from a record label or music management company.
The Commons committee is reportedly expected to hear evidence from BBC chiefs, as well as music industry experts over the coming months.

In 2026, Bulgaria won the contest as singer Dara swept to victory with the song Bangaranga. The 27-year-old singer’s triumph was a first victory for Bulgaria, which only joined Eurovision in 2005 and had sat out the past three editions.

blocks.caption: Dara in Vienna in May. Photograph: Lisa Leutner/Reuters

blocks.text: The UK finished last with Look Mum No Computer, AKA Sam Battle. The YouTuber, who makes his own synthesisers, failed to win over neutral voters with the song Eins, Zwei, Drei. The song received zero points in the public vote, meaning it did not make it into the top 10 in any of the voting countries.

The contest has become increasingly political, primarily over the inclusion of Israel, which has been participating in the event since 1973. Ireland is to boycott the contest for the second year running over the Gaza war. It was one of five countries, along with Iceland, the Netherlands, Spain and Slovenia, that refused to take part in the competition this year in protest against Israel’s participation.

articles.title: Australian man accused of murdering Thai teenager and putting body in suitcase pleads not guilty
articles.summary:
Simon Peter Carman appeared in a Pattaya court on Friday charged with killing Tunchanok Donhomla

An Australian man accused of murdering a Thai teenager and putting her body in a suitcase…

blocks.text: An Australian man accused of murdering a Thai teenager and putting her body in a suitcase pleaded not guilty on Friday in a hearing in the seaside resort city of Pattaya, a court official said.

Simon Peter Carman, 45, was arrested in June after 17-year-old Tunchanok Donhomla was reported missing in Pattaya City, about 150km south-east of Bangkok. A suitcase containing her body was found shortly after.
Police said she died of suffocation.
Carman appeared on Friday at Pattaya provincial court, where he pleaded not guilty to all charges, a court spokesperson said.
He had been charged with murder, concealing a body and taking a minor for indecent purposes. The next court date was set for 12 October.
Police previously said CCTV footage showed him entering a condominium in Pattaya with the girl in the early hours of 25 June, and leaving that evening carrying a large black suitcase.
In a police interrogation video shared online by Thai media, Carman has said he was acting in self-defence because the girl was threatening him with a knife.
The case put the spotlight on Pattaya, which is popular with foreign tourists for its beaches and nightlife, but also has a reputation for sex tourism.

articles.title: Louisiana firefighters find feline native to sub-Saharan Africa while responding to house fire
articles.summary:
The African serval, illegally enclosed in the back yard, was subdued and transferred to an animal welfare facility

Louisiana…

blocks.text: Louisiana firefighters responding to a small house blaze found a wildcat native to sub-Saharan Africa illegally enclosed in the back yard, and an animal welfare agency is now seeking to place the creature in an appropriate environment, according to officials.

Firefighters investigating a report of a minor fire at a home in the suburban New Orleans community of Marrero on Tuesday spotted the cat in question – an African serval – behind the residence in a chain-linked enclosure resembling a cramped baseball batting cage, a spokesperson for the local animal protection services said.

A statement from Jefferson protection and animal welfare services (JPaws) said its director, Michelle Brignac, and humane department supervisor, Victoria Clark, joined firefighters at the scene after they were summoned there. Local laws require an exotic animal permit to legally keep a serval as a pet, and the owner of the home at the center of the case did not have such a document, JPaws spokesperson John McCusker told the Guardian on Thursday.

blocks.caption: An African serval cat being transported after being found in an enclosure in the back yard a of a home. Photograph: John McCusker, JPaws

blocks.text: The statement said Brignac and Clark therefore “subdued the hissing serval and wrangled it” into a transport carrier from its 9ft-by-9ft (7.53-sq-meter) cage that McCusker likened to “a dog kennel”. Brignac and Clark then brought the serval to the JPaws facility in the nearby community of Harvey, according to the statement from the agency, which also shared vivid photographs of the wildcat.

Beside their black spots, svelte physiques and striking facial features, servals are known for their ability to leap as high as about 7ft (2 meters) in the air. So McCusker said JPaws gave the serval an entire room to itself while the agency sought an appropriate refuge for the wildcat, which was born in captivity but whose natural habitat is African grasslands.
Servals share some similarities with domesticated cats that make them immensely popular as pets, including their affinities for grooming themselves, purring, yowling and stalking potential prey.

Nonetheless, they are not easily sustained pets, JPaws’ statement maintained. Servals in captivity do not have the physical space and stimulation needed to engage in normal, healthy behaviors, and they endure chronic stress as a result, the agency’s statement said.

They mark their territory, become aggressive as they mature, cannot be fully house-trained and destroy furniture, and they have been known to barge through walls and doors, according to JPaws. Experts also say servals require a diet and specialized care beyond what house cats need, making them a major responsibility.

JPaws’ statement said the agency would explore having the serval held temporarily at New Orleans’ Audubon zoo. A zoo spokesperson, however, said the institution did not plan to take the serval in and understood JPaws was looking into another arrangement, the details of which were not immediately available on Thursday.
The Marrero serval was the latest of several indicators of the wildcats’ growing popularity, a boom driven in part by social media content creators showing them in videos online.

blocks.caption: Servals mark their territory, become aggressive as they mature and cannot be fully house-trained. Photograph: John Mccusker/John McCusker, JPaws

blocks.text: Cases involving servals have also tended to generate widely read news headlines in North America.
That happened in Ohio in 2023, when officials in the Cincinnati area captured an African serval named Amiry that was spotted in a Cincinnati neighborhood tree and later tested positive for cocaine.

In late 2025, a search for an African serval that escaped a Pennsylvania wildlife center culminated in heartbreak after a motorist fatally struck the wildcat, as Philadelphia’s NBC News affiliated reported.

blocks.caption: The Marrero serval was the latest of several indicators of the wildcats’ growing popularity. Photograph: John Mccusker/John McCusker, JPaws

blocks.text: And the news outlet People reported on authorities in the Canadian city of Vancouver returning an African serval to its owners after it escaped and nestled under a neighbor’s porch in June.

The British Columbia province to which Vancouver belongs had just banned keeping exotic cats such as African servals as pets. But, People reported, the owners of such cats were given until the beginning of May 2027 to apply for permits to legally possess them.

articles.title: Iranian actor Laheh Marzban faces severe threats after Venice film festival speech
articles.summary: Marzban, who won a best actress award for her portrayal of a woman held hostage by her father in Falling House, has received condemnations from authorities after dedicating her prize to ‘the women…

blocks.text: An Iranian actress who won the best newcomer award at the Venice film festival has come under severe attack from the country’s authorities and state media after highlighting the plight of women in Iran in her acceptance speech.

Laleh Marzban last Saturday won the best actress award in the Orizzonti sidebar competition for emerging talent, for her role in Mohsen Gharaei’s Falling House, a film revolving around three generations of women who are incarcerated in their own home by the family’s father.

At the awards gala, Marzban dedicated her prize to “the women of my country who have paid the highest price for even the smallest measure of freedom”. Speaking in Farsi, she added that Iranians were experiencing some of the most difficult days of their lives but should not lose hope.

On Thursday, the Supreme Council of the Cultural Revolution, a conservative-dominated government body appointed by Iran’s supreme leader, issued a statement condemning Marzban’s speech as “presenting a one-sided narrative of Iran’s proud society”.

Referring only to “recent statements and behaviour made at the Venice film festival”, it said reducing Iranian women to “the stereotypes desired by western circles […] is not in line with the awareness-raising mission and social commitment of art”.
The statement has come on the back of a raft of similarly worded attacks in state-affiliated Iranian media, some of which called for the actress to be disciplined by the regime.

Zahra Chekhmaghi, a journalist and presenter associated with the Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB), called Marzban “a two-faced person, […] self-interested, hypocritical, despicable and miserable”, while another IRIB-affiliated media personality, actress Zhila Sadeghi, criticised Marzban for not dedicating her speech instead to the children killed in a US missile strike on an elementary school in Minab on 28 February.

On state TV IRIB, a Qu’ran expert said the actress had been “deceived by the enemy” and called on the government to not let her work in Iran. Another news agency, Student News Network (SNN), urged the ministry of culture to not let Marzban back into the country.

The Iranian reaction to Gharaei’s film and Marzban’s speech appears to mirror the pushback against another film that premiered on the Lido this year, Guardian-produced documentary NAZA, about Israel’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza.

Prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu said this week he would seek new laws allowing Israel to strip citizenship from people who “smear” Israeli soldiers, escalating a campaign against NAZA’s directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor.

Gharaei’s Falling House thematises the collapse of traditional patriarchal family structures in Iran, and men’s efforts to keep them in place by force. Marzban plays twentysomething Ensi, who announces to her family her plans to leave the country and pursue a modelling career in Turkey. In a desperate effort to assert his authority, her father Rashid (Farhad Aslani) locks Ensi and the other female members of the household in their rooms.

Asked after Falling House’s Venice premiere how the film would be received in Iran, Marzban said: “This question is very important for me as an actress, and as all other women in Iran, whether they be doctors, artists, whatever profession women can perform, we can only make one step at the time, one step towards our objective,” she said.
“I have made my small part. I have given my contribution. I really hope many other people can make small steps towards our common objective.”

articles.title: Senators should take public transport once a week --Win Gatchalian
articles.summary: Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said Friday senators should experience commuting via public transportation at least once a week to better understand the situation faced by commuters.

blocks.text: Published September 18, 2026 5:47pm
Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said Friday senators should experience commuting via public transportation at least once a week to better understand the situation faced by commuters.
“That's the only way we will feel and see the needs of our constituents. In fact, dapat kaming mga senador gawin rin namin 'yun to be honest about it,” he said.
(That's the only way we will feel and see the needs of our constituents. In fact, we senators should do the same to be honest about it.)
Gatchalian made the statement during the Senate hearing on the Department of Transportation’s (DOTr) proposed 2027 budget.
He asked Transportation Secretary Giovanni Lopez if the agency’s policy requiring top management to commute once a week is still being implemented. Lopez said he continues to follow the policy.
“Hindi ko pa po binabawi. Ginagawa ko pa rin po. That's once a week...As a matter of fact, we just don't publish it po,” Lopez said.
(I haven't taken it back yet. I'm still doing it. That's once a week...As a matter of fact, we just don't publish it.)
“But to be honest, hindi ko alam kung ginagawa po ng aking mga kasamahan. That's something I cannot check anymore. Pero at least po ginagawa. I have to ask them,” he added.
(But to be honest, I don't know if my colleagues are doing it. That's something I cannot check anymore. But at least it's being done. I have to ask them.)
Gatchalian praised the practice that allows government officials to personally see and experience the challenges faced by commuters.
For Gatchalian, the practice is inspiring.

“I would encourage you and your top management to continue that policy para lang makita natin 'yung totoong situation ng public transportation sector natin. Ako, na-inspire ako doon to be honest about it kasi nakita ko 'yung puso ninyo para sa mga commuters natin. Importante rin 'yun,” he said.

(I would encourage you and your top management to continue that policy just so we can see the real situation of our public transportation sector. I was inspired to be honest about it because I saw your heart for our commuters. That's important too.)

“Hindi naman kailangan mag-Facebook o mag-live o ano.Hindi naman kailangang ganun eh. I think part of the experience and part of the job 'yun. So, sana mag-guilty 'yung mga...nagpaparinig ako. Hindi kayo tine-check ni Secretary pero mag-guilty na lang kayo,” he added.

(You don't have to go on Facebook or go live or anything. You don't have to do that. I think that's part of the experience and part of the job. So, I hope those who are listening to me will feel guilty. The Secretary is not checking you, but you should feel guilty.)
In September last year, Lopez ordered the agency's road and rail officials to take public transportation once a week to better understand the concerns of commuters.
The memorandum aims to implement effective transportation projects and programs, as these officials will experience what daily commuters have to deal with.—AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Bolivia: New cat species discovered by scientists
articles.summary: Genetic data confirmed that the small feline, called "tilcayo" by locals, is a new species of cat. It's the first such discovery in more than 100 years.

image.caption: The Leopardus tilcayo cat was identified through research led by National Geographic Explorer Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz in BoliviaImage: Fernando Faciole/National Geographic/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: Scientists in Bolivia have identified a small wild cat with a leopard-like coat as a previously unknown species.
Local communities call the feline "tilcayo," a nickname that inspired the cat's new scientific designation: Leopardus tilcayo.
Biologist and National Geographic explorer Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz described the discovery as a "remarkable event, because a new wild cat species hasn't been described in 100 years."
The last feline species to be discovered was the Uruguayan pampas cat in 1923.

blocks.caption: The animal is around 18 inches (46 centimeters) long and weighs some 3 pounds (1.4 kilograms)Image: Fernando Faciole/National Geographic/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: What do we know about Leopardus tilcayo?
The cat was found in Bolivia's Yungas forest, a remote region on the eastern slope of the Andes mountains.
The animal measures around 18 inches (46 centimeters) long and weighs around 3 pounds (1.4 kilograms), making it smaller than the average domestic cat.
"Its fur is light brown ... with irregularly shaped rosettes across its body," Nogales-Ascarrunz said.
According to National Geographic, Nogales-Ascarrunz first came upon the animal in 2016 after receiving a call from a local wildlife sanctuary.
The organization said at the time that it had been handed "a weird cat."
"I took a hundred pictures of it," Nogales-Ascarrunz told National Geographic. "I was so fascinated."
It was a few years later that she realized the cat she had photographed was unlike any previously seen.

blocks.caption: National Geographic Explorer Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz led the research that identified Leopardus tilcayoImage: Fernando Faciole/National Geographic/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: Species finds its place in cat family tree
Research on the new species was published this week in the journal Current Biology.

Using genetic analysis in collaboration with geneticist Eduardo Eizirik, co-lead authors Nogales-Ascarrunz and the University of Antwerp's Jonas Lescroart were able to place the feline in its specific category in the cat family tree.
Nogales-Ascarrunz said that a pair of tilcayos have undergone whole-genome sequencing and are the only such creatures found so far.
"So far, it's only been detected in Bolivia" and not "anywhere else on the planet," Nogales-Ascarrunz said.

"Showing the general public that even in a flagship group such as cats ... there are still new species to be discovered may transmit an important message," said Eizirik, who is an evolutionary biologist at the Pontifical Catholic University of Rio Grande do Sul in Brazil.
"There are many undiscovered species out there in the world, and they are at risk of disappearing before we even discover them."

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Poa remains VP Sara’s counsel, defense spokesperson in impeachment trial
articles.summary: Lawyer Michael Poa serves as Duterte's legal counsel and defense team spokesperson in her impeachment trial. He stepped down as the Office of the Vice President’s spokesperson in 2024.

blocks.text: Claim: Lawyer Michael Wesley Poa has vacated his post as Vice President Sara Duterte’s spokesperson.

Why we fact-checked this: The claim was posted on September 9 by the Facebook page “Balita at Kaalaman,” which has more than 219,000 followers. The post has reached over 1,800 reactions as of writing.
The post, labeled as “breaking news,” reads, “Atty Michael Poa binitawan na ni #SaraDuterte after kawawain sa harap ng publiko. Grabe ginagawa sayo niyang praning na amo mo atty.”
(Sara Duterte dropped Atty. Michael Poa after being humiliated in public. That paranoid boss of yours is really putting you through a lot, attorney.)
Two other posts, uploaded on September 2 and 7 respectively, mention that Poa has resigned as Duterte’s spokesperson.

A YouTuber by the channel name “Mike Cervera Vlog” also posted a live stream commentary on August 29 with the title “Atty. Michael Poa nag resign na?!” As of writing, it has reached over 180,000 views and 400 comments.
The posts circulated following reports on September 9 that Duterte appointed lawyer Paolo Panelo as the new spokesperson for the Office of the Vice President (OVP).

The facts: Poa already stepped down as Duterte’s spokesperson on November 5, 2024. However, he remains Duterte’s legal counsel and her defense team’s spokesperson in her impeachment trial. He himself confirmed this in a message to the media on the day Panelo’s appointment was announced.
In a September 10 interview on Bilyonaryo News Channel, Poa clarified his role as he addressed social media speculation that he had been replaced or removed from Duterte’s team.

In November 2024, Poa said the OVP pre-terminated his consultancy contract as spokesperson, describing the move as a “mutual decision.” He added that he could not fulfill his contract as spokesperson because he deemed it difficult to face the media without losing objectivity. At the time, Poa was a resource person in a House panel probe into the OVP’s alleged misuse of funds.

In appointing Panelo as its new spokesperson, the OVP said he will “serve as the official point of communication, representing the views and positions of the Vice President and engaging with the media and public on relevant matters.”
Prosecution’s hostile witness: On September 1, Poa temporarily stepped aside as counsel and spokesperson for the Vice President’s defense team to take the witness stand in the impeachment trial.
He became one of the prosecution’s hostile witnesses, called to testify on Article I of the impeachment articles concerning Duterte’s alleged misuse of confidential funds.

During the trial, Poa faced questions around the use of P112.5 million in confidential funds of the Department of Education (DepEd). In his testimony, Poa said that during his time as DepEd undersecretary and chief of staff, he prepared the agency’s response to the 2024 Commission on Audit findings on DepEd’s use of confidential funds.
However, he said that he was unaware that Duterte’s security officer Colonel Dennis Nolasco handled the funds.

He clarified that his involvement in the confidential funds issue only began when he received the audit memorandum, and that he relied on other officials’ reports to respond to COA’s inquiries on the use of the funds. – Lourence Angelo Marcellana/Rappler.com

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: Philippines school shooting leaves 2 students, gunman dead
articles.summary: Three students were killed in a school shooting in the southern Philippines on Friday, including a 16-year-old suspected gunman who turned the gun on himself, provincial officials said.

image.caption: Emergency personnel walk at a site of a deadly shooting at a school in Banga, South Cotabato, Philippines on Friday. Officials said the young gunman shot several people before killing himself. (Philippine Red Cross/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New
Three students were killed in a school shooting in the southern Philippines on Friday, including a 16-year-old suspected gunman who turned the gun on himself, provincial officials said.
8 others injured in incident in Banga, South Cotabato

Eight others were injured, with four ​in critical condition, and all the victims were ​students aged 14 to 17, said Albert Palencia, mayor of Banga town in South Cotabato, where the shooting took place.

"The suspect supposedly sat beside his ‌friends and told them to go home 'because after lunch, I will be executing my plan.' His friends laughed because the shooter was a known joker," Palencia told Reuters.
"After lunch, he started shooting students. He hit ⁠10 students before killing himself," Palencia added.
South Cotabato governor ⁠Reynaldo ⁠Tamayo urged parents to ensure ​guns were kept out of reach of minors.
"We need to be responsible in storing ​firearms. Gun owners, in particular, ⁠must make sure that minors do not have access to them," Tamayo told Reuters by phone.
"We cannot expect a handful of security personnel to monitor thousands of students. We need to work together because otherwise this will be very difficult for us to ⁠address."
Cluster of school shootings
The incident follows ​two fatal gun incidents since June at schools in the Philippines, ⁠where school shootings were previously ⁠rare.
Last month, a student live-streamed himself shooting and killing another student in a classroom in Zamboanga in the country's south before taking his own ‌life.
In June, at least three students were killed and about 20 others injured in an attack at a public high school in Tacloban, where two classmates opened fire on campus.
The Philippines has relatively strict gun ​ownership regulations, including background checks and psychological evaluation requirements, although illegal firearms remain in circulation.

articles.title: Ombudsman probes Villars, PrimeWater execs over water district deals
articles.summary: he Ombudsman is investigating members of the Villar family, PrimeWater executives and 32 local water district officials over joint venture agreements involving three water districts.

blocks.text: September 18, 2026 | 5:17pm

Senator Mark Villar, former senator Manny Villar, Senator Camille Villar and former senator Cynthia Villar (from left) during the 2025 election campaign. The incumbent lawmakers and their parents are subjects of market manipulation, insider trading and disclosure shortcomings complaints related to their firm, Villar Holdings Corp., filed by the Securities and Exchange Commission.
PNA / Contributed photo

MANILA, Philippines — The Office of the Ombudsman has opened a preliminary investigation into graft and administrative complaints against members of the Villar family, PrimeWater Infrastructure Corp. executives and 32 local water district officials over alleged water service anomalies.

At a press briefing Friday, September 18, Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano said the complaints involve allegedly "grossly disadvantageous" joint venture agreements between PrimeWater and several local water districts.

He also cited PrimeWater's total unpaid obligation of P65,650,708.07 for the use of materials and supplies belonging to the Quezon Metropolitan Water District, San Pedro Water District and Trece Martires City Water District.

Respondents include Sens. Mark and Camille Villar, their brother Manuel Paolo Villar and their parents, former lawmakers Manny and Cynthia Villar, whom the Ombudsman identified as beneficial owners of PrimeWater during the period under investigation.
The Ombudsman also included PrimeWater president Fe Reblancos and vice president Romeo Sabater in the complaints.

The complaints also involve the general managers of three local water districts: Enrico Pasumbal of Quezon Metropolitan Water District, Guillermo Pili of San Pedro Water District and Juliet Ocampo of Trece Martires City Water District.
Other respondents include:

items: Five members of the joint venture selection committee of the Quezon Metropolitan Water District
Five members of the Quezon Metropolitan Water District Board of Directors
Six members of the joint venture selection committee of the San Pedro Water District
Two members of the San Pedro Water District Board of Directors
Five members of the joint venture selection committee of the Trece Martires City Water District
Six members of the Trece Martires City Water District Board of Directors

blocks.text: The Ombudsman is looking into potential violations of Sections 3(e) and 3(g) of Republic Act No. 3019, or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act.
"Ito 'yung nakukuha nating mga complaints galing sa ating mga kababayan na hindi malinis at may interupsyon sa tubig na nakukuha nila," Clavano said.
(These are the complaints we receive from the public about unclean water and interrupted water service.)

The Ombudsman said the case stemmed from a report it received from the Office of the Government Corporate Counsel, which showed that 75 local water districts entered into joint venture agreements with PrimeWater from 2015 to 2022.
"This is the initial list and there are still more water districts under investigation, and expectantly, more cases in the pipelines," Clavano said.

articles.title: Andrew Hastie says AI advised him to reply ‘congratulations!’ to man who planned to end life with assisted dying
articles.summary:
Liberal MP speaks of AI’s shortcomings as cyber chief tells inquiry the tech is needed to fend off ‘highly capable malicious cyber actors’

  • Get our

blocks.text: When a man with a terminal illness wrote to his local MP Andrew Hastie, telling him he planned on ending his own life with voluntary assisted dying, Microsoft Copilot suggested Hastie reply with “congratulations!”, “great to hear from you” or “that is wonderful news!”.
Hastie shared the episode at a parliamentary inquiry on Friday to underline the shortcomings of the American-run software as he called for AI run by Australians.
The hearing offered the some of the most detailed explanations of the Albanese government’s desire to bring Anthropic and OpenAI to Australia, in the face of calls to slow them down or shut them out.
The defence establishment told the inquiry that cutting the companies out could be catastrophic.
Abigail Bradshaw, the director general of the Australian Signals Directorate, said her agents needed advanced AI every day to fend off “highly capable malicious cyber actors”.

“If a digital adversary has access to newer, more capable models than we do, they may be able to identify and exploit vulnerabilities in systems and networks before we can identify them,” Bradshaw said.
But Australia’s top cyber-intelligence agency is “entirely reliant” on US-housed processing and would “dramatically” lose capability if cut off in a conflict, Bradshaw said.

The defence department’s chief AI officer, Chris Crozier, said the government was already trying to keep its tech needs local, contracting Google to build a series of interlinked datacentres spread across the country and disconnected from the US.
“Somebody can’t wake up and have a bad day and decide they’re going to turn it off,” Crozier said.
“We do not want to be using AI tool sets that are located offshore … we want the compute, we want the application, we want the data, we want the decision making, all based in Australia.”
Bringing big tech into the country would make the job much easier, he said, and not just by allowing the army to protect and maintain its datacentres.
The Office of AI, set up in the prime minister’s department, said bringing firms under Australian law would make it easier for local law enforcement to combat threats on the platforms.
Tight conditions on access could also materially improve Australia’s chances of using and defending itself with the best AI tools in the world, the inquiry heard.
“We will get more assured access, earlier access, more detailed technical access, and better integration with technical experts at the frontier,” Bradshaw said.
These would be assured by strict requirements on any top developers looking to train models in Australia, such as demanding government oversight and early access to advanced models, she suggested.

blocks.caption: The Australian Signals Directorate chief Abigail Bradshaw. Photograph: Mike Bowers/The Guardian

blocks.text: The government is already planning to set the rules for companies that come here. It is consulting on standards that would force AI companies to report issues and breaches and potentially reserve some computational power for local research.
Large datacentres will have to engage with communities, build away from schools and homes, and underwrite new renewables in most states.
after newsletter promotion
Another pillar of the standards – copyright law – is yet to be settled, with AI developers refusing to train models here without law reform.

A proposal to give the companies access to everything Australians create online by default sparked a wave of backlash from creatives, who say the companies could pay for local licensing deals to access Australian content.

But Jenna Priestly, the assistant secretary at the attorney general’s department, on Friday confirmed looser copyright laws would also affect AI access to foreign-made content distributed in Australia.
She said the companies wanted to train models on “maybe billions” of pieces of information and claimed it was practically “impossible” to make deals with every rights holder.

“As Australia’s copyright framework protects not only copyright material that’s Australian in origin, but worldwide, I think it is a fairly large number that [companies] would need to go and strike deals with,” Priestly said.

The Greens senator David Shoebridge, who is among those fighting calls for copyright reform and demanding a pause on AI development, on Friday said Labor had refused him a seat on the inquiry committee.

Labor ministers have spent the week meeting with OpenAI’s vice-president, and Anthropic’s special envoy Jeff Bleich, who this week suggested Australia had just months to bring in effective regulation.

The attorney general’s department told Friday’s hearing the shape and timing of any copyright reform was yet to be decided. But the prime minister’s department said Anthony Albanese wanted draft laws on the broader AI standards by the end of 2026.
Australia’s chance for influence on and special access to the models could be at risk by a delay, Bradshaw said.
“Decisions around training are a matter of urgency,” she said. “I think it is inevitable that those providers will look at other places to locate.”

articles.title: She pressed charges against a Mountie for sex assault, but says court delays robbed her of justice
articles.summary: A sexual assault case against RCMP Const. William McNutt was dropped because of delays in the justice system. The complainant says if restorative justice had been an option, she would have taken it.

image.caption: The complainant in a sexual assault case that was dropped due to court delays says the criminal justice system is failing some complainants, and that restorative justice should be an option available to them in Nova Scotia. (Brian MacKay/CBC)

blocks.text: Editor's note: This story includes details of an alleged sexual assault and might affect those who have experienced​ ​​​sexual violence.

A Nova Scotia woman who alleges she was sexually assaulted by an RCMP officer says the national framework intended to ensure timely trials is failing some survivors — and that alternatives to criminal trials, such as restorative justice, should be an option.

The case involving the officer she accused, RCMP Const. William McNutt, 41, was recently thrown out due to delays in the justice system. It was the first of three criminal cases involving allegations of sexual assault against McNutt.
CBC News is not naming the woman because of a court-ordered publication ban on her identity.
The woman alleged that in early 2023, McNutt choked her and threatened to rape her if she did not perform oral sex on him.

“I had to make a split-second decision how to get out of this because I'm looking up at this six-foot-eight man who's a police officer in a position of power, essentially threatening to rape me,” she said in an interview. “So ultimately I complied with it to get myself out of the situation.”
She says for months afterward, she struggled to come to terms with what happened. Eventually, in July 2024, McNutt was charged with sexual assault, choking and uttering threats.
McNutt pleaded not guilty, and the allegations have not been tested in court. McNutt's lawyer declined a request for comment.

The woman says the criminal justice process — which involved retelling and reliving the alleged assault and having her credibility questioned by McNutt's lawyer — affected her mental health to the extent that at one point, it was unclear whether she would be able to carry on with the process.
“It's constantly retraumatizing you and bringing everything back up to the surface … and it's just never-ending. Like it controls your life and it eats you alive.”
Then, on May 26, two days before the trial was set to begin, the process abruptly came to a halt.

Judge Ian Hutchison ruled that McNutt’s right to a trial within a reasonable amount of time had been violated, citing a 2016 Supreme Court ruling known as the Jordan framework. It stipulates that criminal trials must be completed within 18 months for a provincial court and 30 months for a Superior Court.
Hutchison issued a stay of proceedings, saying McNutt’s case would have gone on for more than 24 months by the time the trial was scheduled to end.

“It knocks the wind out of you,” the complainant says. “The system's failing, essentially. Like people in my position go through this really gruelling process and then they're just left with essentially nothing.”
“It seems very broken.”
The woman says she does not feel she got any justice through the court process, and that if restorative justice had been an option, she likely would have taken it.
“Just to make them sit there and listen to, you know, you hurt me,” she says. “Just to get to say my piece … it just would have given me a bit of my sense of self back."

Restorative justice is a process that aims to address the harm caused to a complainant, and sometimes involves bringing together the complainant and accused to communicate about the causes, impacts and circumstances of the incident. The process can lead to accountability measures for the accused and supports to address the underlying causes of the incident.
But, unlike in some other provinces and territories, restorative justice is not available in sexual assault cases in Nova Scotia.
The province implemented a moratorium in 2000 after hearing concerns about survivor safety, power imbalances, appropriate training, screening and community supports for participants.
Jennifer Llewellyn is a law professor at Dalhousie University who specializes in restorative justice.

Llewellyn says while the concerns that led to the moratorium should be front of mind, a lot of work has been done in the fields of gender-based violence and alternative justice since the moratorium came into effect, and it is time to make restorative justice available to survivors of sexual violence.

“The shame, the alienation, the isolation that comes from being a victim of gender-based violence and sexualized violence is real,” Llewellyn says. “And the solution to that comes from being placed at the centre, your needs being placed at the centre of the process that seeks to respond to those harms.”

A new bill that came into effect across Canada this summer could improve options and outcomes for survivors of sexual assault. Bill C-16 mandates courts to consider alternatives to staying proceedings when a case comes up against its Jordan deadline.
It also explicitly gives a right for victims to have their interests considered in the timely resolution of matters.
While it stops short of saying victims must have access to restorative justice options, it says victims have a right to get information about restorative justice.
Llewellyn says her reading of the legislation is that “we can't take that decision away from them entirely in all cases.”
“I think we're in a moment now where Nova Scotia is well positioned … to rethink the moratorium and to think about how to move forward with a restorative pathway for those who choose it,” she says.
The Justice Department did not directly answer a question from CBC News about whether the province is reconsidering the moratorium.
"We continue to listen to those most affected, including through the Ministers’ Table on Gender-Based Violence," a statement said.

"This is a complex and important issue, and good public policy is informed by the voices of Nova Scotians, survivors, advocates and community partners. We continue to consider these perspectives as part of our ongoing work in this area."
Since 2016, 23 cases of sexual assault-related charges in Nova Scotia have been stayed due to delays and the Jordan deadline.

Nova Scotia Justice Minister Scott Armstrong was not made available for an interview. A department spokesperson sent CBC News a statement attributed to him that said reducing delays in the justice systems is a "top priority."

According to the statement, the province has taken steps to ensure matters proceed in a timely manner, including adding public prosecution service staff to help reduce court backlogs, creating a bail court to free up capacity in courtrooms for trials, and modernizing courts through virtual appearances and courtroom technology.
“Progress is being made and we know there is more work to do to make sure Nova Scotians have a timely, fair and accessible justice system,” the statement says.
The woman whose case was stayed says more change is needed to allow complainants to feel that they received justice.

"When you don't get that, it puts you right back in that place where you were in that vulnerable position where someone's hurting you and you don't get to have a say," she says. "You don't get to choose what you're doing or how you're responding to it. You're just surviving."
No appeal was filed in the woman’s case.
McNutt was acquitted of sexual assault charges in a case involving a second complainant. An appeal has been filed, and the case is next due in Amherst Supreme court on Nov. 4.
Another case, involving a third complainant who alleges McNutt sexually assaulted her, is scheduled in Shubenacadie provincial court on Oct. 19. He has pleaded not guilty.
McNutt has been suspended without pay from his role at the RCMP pending the outcome of the criminal trials and an internal code of conduct process.

If you’re in immediate danger or fear for your safety or that of others around you, please call 911. For support in your area, you can look for crisis lines and local services via the Ending Sexual Violence Association of Canada database. ​​

articles.title: Oktoberfest 2026: Everything you need to know
articles.summary: This year, AI will be used to manage overcrowded situations. Find all the numbers surrounding the fest — including the price of water!

image.caption: Oktoberfest attracts millions of visitors every yearImage: Wolfgang Maria Weber/IMAGO

blocks.text: On Saturday, September 19, at noon, Oktoberfest will once again open with the ceremonial tapping of the keg, during which the mayor of Munich drives a tap into the first wooden barrel of beer and calls out "O'zapft is," a Bavarian phrase that translates to "It's tapped."
His call will be followed by 12 gunshots, a signal that lets all festival tents know that they can start serving beer.
More than 6 million people are expected at the world's largest Volksfest, which runs this year through October 4.
Oktoberfest: What to know about 'the best party in Germany'
Expanded security measures to prevent overcrowding
The festival grounds are enormous: Oktoberfest takes place on Munich's Theresienwiese, a 34.5-hectare site roughly the size of 48 soccer fields.
But crowds can swell, especially on weekends — sometimes to dangerous levels.
Last year, officials had to temporarily close the entrances.

One reason is that nearly all 38 beer tents operate in two or three reservation shifts. When one group of guests leaves and the next arrives at the 14 large tents — which each accommodate several thousand people — huge numbers of visitors end up trying to enter and exit at the same time.
That's how, on one Saturday afternoon at last year's Oktoberfest, the crowds became so dense that movement temporarily came to a standstill. The crush caused some visitors to panic.
To prevent that from happening again, the city of Munich has overhauled its security plan for this year's festival.
Twenty-six new cameras, in addition to 56 police cameras, will monitor the grounds, while an AI system will analyze visitor flows and issue alerts if areas become overcrowded.

blocks.caption: Around 300,000 people were at Oktoberfest simultaneously on the second Saturday of the festival in 2025Image: Frank Hoermann/SVEN SIMON/picture alliance

blocks.text: A newly established coordination center is also intended to improve communication between security agencies and event organizers.
Organizers and police have drawn up a plan to defend against drones over the grounds, though no details have been disclosed.
In addition, 600 police officers will be deployed on site.
Oktoberfest is famous worldwide, but most visitors are local
Oktoberfest may be known around the world as an international tourist attraction, but most of its visitors don't travel very far to get there.
A study commissioned by the city of Munich last year found that the festival remains overwhelmingly regional.

blocks.caption: Statistically speaking, two international guests sit at every 10-person table in the festival tentsImage: Maryam Majd/REUTERS

blocks.text: In 2025, 41% of visitors came from Munich, another 25% from the surrounding area and 9% from elsewhere in the region. In all, three-quarters of Oktoberfest's roughly 6.5 million visitors came from Bavaria. Another 4% came from elsewhere in Germany.

About 21% of visitors — roughly 1.35 million people — traveled from abroad. Americans made up the largest group of international visitors, accounting for just under 20% of the total, or more than 270,000 people. Italians were next, at just over 13%.
Beer prices rise again
Cannabis is banned throughout the festival grounds.

Alcohol, on the other hand, is available in whatever quantities visitors are willing — and able — to pay for. A Mass, the traditional 1-liter mug of beer served at Oktoberfest, costs between €14.80 and €15.90 ($17-$18.25) this year, only slightly more than last year.
A liter of table water comes in at a hefty €11, although the grounds also have several free drinking water fountains.
Visitors planning to enjoy one of Oktoberfest's many rides would be wise to stay relatively sober. Tickets cost anywhere from just under €5 to €14.

Germany's traditional fairground culture was officially added to the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2026, and that tradition remains very much alive at the 191st Oktoberfest. According to organizers, about 90% of the festival's more than 130 fairground operators can trace their roots back to the 19th century.
The festival remains decidedly traditional when it comes to payment, too: Many vendors still accept cash only. Visitors caught without any can withdraw money from ATMs on the grounds.
Dirndl or lederhosen for Oktoberfest?
Then there's the question of what to wear.
Bavarians who take pride in doing things properly generally show up in local traditional dress.

blocks.caption: Traditional garb can be seen at the annual breweries' paradeImage: Felix Hörhager/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: The dirndl is the traditional dress worn by women and girls, which consists of close-fitting bodice with a low neckline, a blouse worn under the bodice, a wide high-waisted skirt and an apron.
Men wear lederhosen, the traditional leather shorts or knee-length breeches with suspenders.

For those who are not Bavarian, lederhosen and dirndls are certainly an option, but they're by no means required. Munich's event marketing department, Simply Munich, advises first-time visitors to consider renting traditional garb rather than buying it.

Be aware that locals find cheap imitations of traditional dress off-putting, as Simply Munich points out: "If you want to avoid wry looks, steer clear of Seppl hats, 'leather pants' made of cloth and garish mini plastic dirndls. With jeans and a checkered shirt, you'll definitely be more suitably dressed."
This article was originally written in German.

articles.title: AFP backs development of expeditionary navy
articles.summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Friday expressed support for the development of an expeditionary navy capable of conducting missions beyond home waters, saying this is necessary for the…

blocks.text: Published September 18, 2026 4:44pm

The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Friday expressed support for the development of an expeditionary navy capable of conducting missions beyond home waters, saying this is necessary for the country's defense as an archipelagic nation.

Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad, AFP spokesperson for West Philippine Sea, said the AFP fully supports the vision by Defense Secretary Gilberto "Gibo" Teodoro Jr. on the necessity of developing an expeditionary Navy.

"As an archipelagic nation that relies on the seas as our lifeblood, the shift toward a blue-water, expeditionary capability is a natural and necessary evolution of our national defense posture," Trinidad said in a statement.
He said the initiative is aligned with the Comprehensive Archipelagic Defense Concept (CADC).

Trinidad said this move calls for the projection of capabilities to protect Philippine territory, defend sovereignty, secure sovereign rights across maritime borders, and safeguard sea lanes of communication.

According to Trinidad, an expeditionary naval force would allow the Philippine Navy to maintain a persistent presence at sea, conduct long-range maritime patrols, project deterrence across the country's maritime domain, and respond to the needs of Filipinos abroad.
Teodoro earlier shared the goal of developing the Philippine Navy into becoming expeditionary to protect Philippine national interests, even in the high seas.
"We need an expeditionary navy to be able to protect Filipinos, seafarers, and Filipino vessels in the high seas, alike and alongside like-minded countries,” he said. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Weather tracker: Thunderstorms hit Spain as Japan braces for typhoon
articles.summary:
At least one person dead as stormy weather causes severe flooding in Barcelona and Valencia

Intense and slow-moving thunderstorms broke out on Wednesday afternoon across parts of eastern…

blocks.text: Intense and slow-moving thunderstorms broke out on Wednesday afternoon across parts of eastern Spain, bringing some severe flooding and killing at least one person.

Storms first struck over the Castilla-La Mancha regionduring the afternoon before passing over Spain’s east coast, becoming very slow-moving and continuing overnight. Torrential rainfall, strong winds and large hail were reported in Valencia and Barcelona, causing widespread flooding in both cities. Weather stations west of Barcelona recorded some of the highest totals with more than 100mm (4in) of rain falling in the space of a few hours, and locally 70mm in just 30 minutes in the early hours of Thursday morning. Cars and roads were submerged, and flights were cancelled across the region.

Wednesday’s La Liga fixture between Levante and Athletic Club had to be postponed due to flooding at the Estadio Ciudad de Valencia. On Thursday rescuers found the body of a man near Olivella, west of Barcelona, after his car was swept away in the waters. Spain’s east coast is susceptible to extreme rainfall during the autumn months, as experienced in 2024, when devastating flash floods killed more than 200 people in Valencia. With the Mediterranean Sea reaching record temperatures, this is providing extra fuel and moisture to thunderstorms, making flooding more likely.

In New Jersey in the US on Sunday, the Racefaster half marathon was disrupted due to extreme rainfall and a partly submerged course. Runners had to wade through chest-deep waters at times as 50mm-100mm of rain fell. Despite the flooding, 250 people managed to finish the race. Flooding was also reported to the north-east in Connecticut and Rhode Island, where up to 190mm of rain was recorded in a 36-hour period.

Tropical Storm Dujuan, currently over the open west Pacific Ocean, will move north-west on a track towards Japan over the coming days. It is forecast to intensify into a category one typhoon on Friday. The joint typhoon warning centre is forecasting that Dujuan will skirt past the southeast coast of Japan, potentially affecting Tokyo and the surrounding areas.

articles.title: Marital infidelity alone not punishable under Anti-VAWC Law -- SC
articles.summary: It must be proven that psychological violence was inflicted for marital infidelity to be punishable under the Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004, the Supreme Court (SC)…

blocks.text: Published September 18, 2026 4:36pm

It must be proven that psychological violence was inflicted for marital infidelity to be punishable under the Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004, the Supreme Court (SC) reiterated.

In a 16-page decision, the SC Second Division said this as it affirmed the conviction of a husband for violation of Section 5(i) of the Anti-VAWC Act, finding that the emotional anguish inflicted on his partner was established.
“The emotional or mental anguish of AAA and BBB due to the marital infidelity of XXX was proved beyond reasonable doubt,” the High Court said.

“AAA clearly narrated the trauma, humiliation, and depression she experienced due to XXX’s marital infidelity to the extent that she attempted to take her own life, not just one, but several times,” it added.

Citing a previous ruling, the SC said that marital infidelity per se is not punishable under the law. Instead, what the law penalizes is the psychological violence causing mental or emotional suffering upon the victim.
The SC noted that depending on the circumstances, an illicit relationship may or may not be causing mental or emotional anguish on the wife.
In the present case, the husband and wife married in 1999 and had two children.

The SC said their marital problems started in 2009 when the husband began to grow distant. A year later, he sent his wife text messages that would seek the nullity of their marriage and that he wanted to start a new life alone.
However, the wife later discovered that her husband was living with another woman, leading her to file a case with the Regional Trial Court (RTC).

During the trial, the psychologist found that the wife was suffering from depression, feelings of inferiority, sleep problems, had difficulty concentrating, and had problems relating with others. The psychologist linked these to the husband’s abandonment.
The RTC and the Court of Appeals found him guilty.
The SC affirmed the ruling.

“Marital infidelity destroys the stability and unity of the family at its core, shatters the self-worth and trust of the betrayed spouse, and fosters deep-seated trauma borne of emotional turmoil and related mental health issues,” the SC said.
“There is thus no question that marital infidelity, especially that which causes mental and emotional suffering oh the innocent spouse, cannot, in any degree, be condoned by the Court,” it added.
Meanwhile, in a dissenting opinion, Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen agreed that marital infidelity should not be considered as an act of violence under the law by itself.

However, he said that the prosecution failed to prove that the petitioner’s marital infidelity was precisely done to inflict mental or emotional anguish on his wife. He said that it appears the husband left the wife because he fell out of law.
Leonen said that the language of the law is clear that “deliberate intent to inflict mental or emotional anguish should be shown.”
“My vote to acquit petitioner should not be construed as an approval of marital infidelity, nor should this be used as an excuse to disregard one's commitments,” he said.

“There is no dispute that petitioner's wife experienced emotional suffering upon learning about petitioner's infidelity. However, emotional suffering is not sufficient to warrant a conviction for psychological violence,” he added. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: ‘We have something that will kill Elliott’: Icac questions former Labor councillor over message
articles.summary: Sharangan Maheswaran denies message he received about NSW minister was related to work for fugitive property developer

blocks.text: A former Labor councillor says he had a “common interest” with a conservative Liberal operative, but denied that a message he received about damaging the reputation of NSW Liberal minister David Elliott was related to political work for a fugitive property developer, an inquiry has heard.

Sharangan Maheswaran told the Independent Commission Against Corruption (Icac) on Friday that a message sent to him by lobbyist Jeremy Greenwood claiming “We have something that will kill Elliott” did not relate to work by Greenwood’s company Beckington for Jean Nassif.
Maheswaran, who is no longer a councillor, was a lawyer to property developer Nassif and became an executive at his company, Toplace, in September 2020.

Icac is examining whether Liberal figures Greenwood, Charles Perrottet and Christian Ellis anticipated receiving $2m in prohibited donations from Nassif in exchange for political outcomes, including damage to the career of former NSW Liberal minister and centre-right faction member David Elliott, who had opposed Toplace developments. Greenwood, Perrottet and Nassif have denied that Nassif paid for political outcomes.
On Friday, Dwyer took Maheswaran to a message Greenwood wrote to him in February 2020 in which he said: “We have something that will kill Elliot.”

Maheswaran replied: “Your ears must be ringing. I just picked up the phone to let you know that I’ve got something decent, and the SMH [Sydney Morning Herald] is going to fire up re [centre-right Liberal MP Alex] Hawke this week off the back of an ALP bill to ban developers.”
Dwyer put it to Maheswaran that the messages showed he shared “a common interest with Beckington in terms of damaging the reputation of David Elliott”.
Maheswaran said he “had a common interest with Mr Greenwood in relation to the Hawke faction of the Liberal party”, but rejected the suggestion the messages related to work by Beckington for Nassif.
When he was asked if Nassif had told him that Elliott had objected to Toplace proposals, Maheswaran said “this is a new invention by Mr Nassif”.

Dwyer asked him if he “seriously contend[ed] to the commission that Jean Nassif never told you that David Elliott was objecting to his proposals”, asking if Maheswaran was suggesting that Nassif had lied to the commission.

Maheswaran said: “His complaint, up to 2025, as I understood it, was that Mr Elliott was backgrounding against him to the media and to various public officials and government officials, but it wasn’t specifically related to any planning process.”

Asked again if Nassif had lied, Maheswaran said “absolutely”. He was shown a draft statutory declaration he sent to a lawyer in 2022 in which he wrote that Nassif had spoken to Elliott about his opposition to a Toplace developments.
Dwyer put it to Maheswaran that he was “happy to assist him [Nassif] with the political outcome he was seeking, which was to get rid of Mr Elliott”.
“I don’t think that was an objective that Mr Nassif was seeking at that point in time,” he responded.

The inquiry heard that Maheswaran came to know Nassif through his daughter Ashlyn Nassif, who was sentenced to a six-month community corrections order earlier this month after pleading guilty to providing false or misleading information to obtain a $150m construction loan from Westpac.
Maheswaran said he was subcontracted to do work for Toplace through Ashlyn Nassif and her sister Evelyn Helou’s law firm EA Legal in late 2019, through another company, Anwalt Pty Ltd.
after newsletter promotion
But he took issue with Dwyer’s suggestion that he and Anwalt were one and the same.

He said: “That’s nonsensical from a corporation’s perspective, from a commercial perspective, from any sort of understanding of contractual law, I’m sorry, Dr Dwyer, I’m speaking in terms of as I understand the world.”
“No problem,” replied Dwyer. Under questioning, Maheswaran accepted that he was the only shareholder and employee of Anwalt at the time.
Dwyer said: “So the only person doing any actual work was you, correct?”
“At that point in time, yes,” said Maheswaran.

Maheswaran told the commission he was paid $1.4m by Toplace between 2020 and 2023, but said he had not disclosed that he was a close associate of a property developer when he nominated for council in 2021, which Dwyer said was required by law.

Icac is investigating whether Maheswaran and fellow Labor Strathfield councillor Karen Pensabene engaged in conduct towards former mayor Matthew Blackmore in a way “that involves the dishonest or partial exercise of their official functions and/or a breach of public trust, including conduct which could involve blackmail” and possible breaches of the Surveillance Devices Act.

When Icac announced its public hearings, Maheswaran told Guardian Australia: “I have every confidence that my actions will be regarded by the public and by any fair tribunal to be lawful and entirely in the public interest.”
On Friday, the inquiry heard that Pensabene had been excused from her summons for medical reasons.
The inquiry continues.

articles.title: ‘We demand the truth’: Olga Tokarczuk and JM Coetzee lead calls for proof of life of disappeared Eritrean writers
articles.summary:
More than 180 writers sign letter renewing calls for information on 12 authors detained incommunicado since 2001 crackdown on free speech by Isaias Afwerki

More than 180 writers have signed…

blocks.text: More than 180 writers have signed a letter to Eritrean president Isaias Afwerki calling for proof of life for 12 writers arrested in 2001.

Nobel laureates Olga Tokarczuk and JM Coetzee join prominent writers including Colm Tóibín, Elif Shafak, Isabel Allende, Ben Okri, Yann Martel, Kamila Shamsie and Tsitsi Dangarembga in signing the letter dated 18 September, marking 25 years since a government crackdown on the independent press. “Within days, Eritrea’s free press and the nation’s independent voices were systematically crushed,” opens the letter.
It lists 12 writers who have been held incommunicado since 2001, including the poet Amanuel Asrat and playwright and journalist Dawit Isaak.

“The families of these writers, the Eritrean people and the global literary community have been met with a painful and unlawful silence,” continues the statement. “To withhold all information regarding their health, location, and survival is a violation of international law and an act of cruelty.”

Along with Asrat and Isaak, the other writers named in the letter are Dawit Habtemichael, Fessehaye “Joshua” Yohannes, Mattewos Habteab, Medhanie Haile, Sahle “Wedi-ltay” Tsegazeab, Said Abdelkadir, Said Idris “Abu Are”, Seyoum Tsehaye, Temesgen Ghebreyesus and Yousif Mohammed Ali. Six of the writers were profiled in the Guardian in 2015.
The letter, signed by 188 writers in total, calls for “immediate, verified proof of life for all arbitrarily detained Eritrean writers and critics”.

Other signatories include Andrei Kurkov, Anthony Doerr, Chloe Aridjis, Lauren Groff, Lemn Sissay, Maaza Mengiste, Madeleine Thien, Margaret Busby, Max Porter, Philippe Sands, Preti Taneja, Tice Cin and Viv Groskop.

“Mr President, Eritrea’s future must be built with its brightest minds, not based on their suppression,” the letter adds. “No writer or journalist should be disappeared for peacefully expressing their views.”
Eritrea operates as a repressive dictatorship under Afwerki, with no national elections held since independence in 1993.
“We remain in solidarity with our missing colleagues, and we will not cease our efforts until they are free,” the letter concludes.

PEN International will attempt delivery of the letter at the Eritrean embassy in London at 10am on Friday. Earlier this year, the organisation launched a petition, open to the public, which also calls for proof of life.

“Twenty-five years is an unbearable length of time for any family to live without knowing whether a loved one is alive,”, said Burhan Sönmez, president of PEN International. “These writers have not disappeared from our memory. We will continue to speak their names, and we will continue to demand the truth about what happened to them.”

articles.title: At least one dead and multiple injured in Philippines school shooting
articles.summary: At least one person is believed to have died and several injured after the shooting in Banga in Mindanao province.

blocks.text: A shooting at a high school in southern Philippines has left at least one person dead and several injured.
The incident happened on Friday afternoon at Banga National High School in South Cotabato, in Mindanao province.
Local media and officials have reporting conflicting casualty figures. The identities of the shooter and the victims have not been confirmed.
The Department of Education said in a statement that it was "deeply concerned by the reported shooting incident".

"Our immediate priority is the safety and well-being of our learners, teachers and school personnel," the statement said, adding it was coordinating with authorities to verify the incident and provide necessary support.
"We urge everyone to remain calm and refrain from sharing unverified information as authorities continue their investigation."

South Cotabato Governor Reynaldo Tamayo told reporters earlier that one person died and four people had been hospitalised. He did not give details on the identity of the shooter, nor did he indicate the shooter was among the dead or injured.
Local media have been reporting much higher casualty figures, citing other Philippine authorities.
Classes have been suspended "in all levels in the entire municipality of Banga" due to the shooting, the Banga disaster management authorities said in a statement.
The Philippine Red Cross said it has deployed medical teams to help out in the aftermath of the shooting.
Police are at the site investigating the shooting, local media reported.
Gun crime is not uncommon in the Philippines, which has one of the highest rates of gun ownership in the region - though school shootings remain rare.

In June, three students were killed and more were injured after their peers opened fire at a high school in central Philippines. Investigators believed the deadly shooting had been motivated by a "grudge" over bullying.

articles.title: NTF-WPS condemns China's ramming of BFAR vessel off Palawan
articles.summary: The National Task Force for the West Philippine Sea (NTF-WPS) on Friday condemned the China Coast Guard (CCG) for reportedly ramming a Philippine Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR)…

blocks.text: Published September 18, 2026 4:26pm

The National Task Force for the West Philippine Sea (NTF-WPS) on Friday condemned the China Coast Guard (CCG) for reportedly ramming a Philippine Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) vessel on a civilian mission.

"We remain resolute in protecting the rights and welfare of our fisherfolk and ensuring that lawful government missions in the WPS continue without intimidation or coercion," the NTF-WPS said in a statement.

"The NTF-WPS calls on China to cease dangerous and unlawful actions that endanger lives at sea. We will continue to exercise our rights under international law with restraint, professionalism, and firm commitment to the security and dignity of the Filipino people," it added.

CCG vessel 21585 rammed the BRP Datu Magat Salamat while the Philippine vessel was carrying out its maritime patrol and fuel subsidy mission around 6.36 nautical miles north-northwest of Abad Santos Shoal and about 54 nautical miles from Palawan's coast.
This area is within the Philippines' exclusive economic zone (EEZ).

According to the Task Force, the BFAR vessel was conducting a lawful civilian mission when the Chinese vessel repeatedly made hazardous maneuvers before deliberately making contact with the Philippine ship.
The collision damaged the BFAR vessel and put its civilian crew at risk, according to the NTF-WPS.

The BFAR vessel sustained damage to its starboard side, including bent, broken and detached railings, deformed metal stanchions and support structures, and displaced deck fixtures and equipment, according to the PCG.

For the NTF-WPS, China's actions constituted a serious breach of the 1972 Convention on the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea (COLREGs), the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), and the 2016 Arbitral Award.

Tensions continue as Beijing claims almost all of the South China Sea, a conduit for more than $3 trillion of annual shipborne commerce, including parts claimed by the Philippines, Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Brunei.
Parts of the South China Sea that fall within Philippine territory have been renamed by the government as West Philippine Sea to reinforce the country's claim.

The West Philippine Sea refers to the maritime areas on the western side of the Philippine archipelago including Luzon Sea and the waters around, within and adjacent to the Kalayaan Island Group and Bajo de Masinloc.
In 2016, the Permanent Court of Arbitration in the Hague ruled in favor of the Philippines over China's claims in the South China Sea, saying that it had "no legal basis."
China has refused to recognize the decision. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Burnham will meet Irish PM as UK bids to get exemptions from EU’s ‘Made in Europe’ plan – UK politics live
articles.summary:
It will be the first time the PM uses No 10 North to host an overseas visit while the chancellor will be in Dublin meeting with EU finance ministers

Good morning. On Monday, at her summit in…

blocks.text: Burnham to meet Irish PM at No 10 North as UK bids to get exemptions from EU’s ‘Made in Europe’ plan

Good morning. On Monday, at her summit in Cardiff with the leaders of the SNP and Plaid Cymru, Mary Lou McDonald, the Sinn Féin president, joked about Liverpool being the 33rd county of Ireland. Andy Burnham is basically a Scouser; he was born in Liverpool and supports a Liverpool football team, despite being brought up in Culcheth, a village mid-way between Liverpool and Manchester, which made him enough of a Manc to be the city’s mayor. He also has Irish ancestry, and so the mood should be very cordial today when he hosts Micheál Martin, the taoiseach (Irish PM) at No 10 North in Manchester this morning.

It is the first time that Burnham has used No 10 North to host an overseas visit, which should help a bit his efforts to establish that No 10 North is a proper government power base, and not just a branch office.
And, in its overnight release about the visit, No 10 says it is part of a deliberate attempt by Burnham to use meetings with overseas leaders to highlight parts of the UK outside London. No 10 says:

double quotation markThe historic visit to No 10 North comes as the prime minister shines a spotlight on towns up and down the country, days after he hosted Canadian prime minister Mark Carney in Liverpool and Nato secretary general Mark Rutte in Oxford.
No 10 also points out that, when Burnham met Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the Ukrainian president, they were at Portsmouth.

It should be a friendly meeting. When Burnham was mayor of Greater Manchester, he had several meetings with Martin, including in Ireland, and when Burnham became PM Martin issued a statement praising him as someone who was “a great champion of deeper links between Ireland and Britain”. No 10 says the talks will focus on “shared objectives including boosting trade, supporting Ukraine, and working with the European Union as Ireland continues its presidency of the EU”. After the formal meetings, the two leaders will visit an Irish community centre.

While Burnham and Martin are meeting in Manchester, John Healey, the chancellor, will be in Dublin where he has been invited to an informal meeting of Ecofin, the meeting of EU finance ministers. And it is not just a social meeting. The UK is desperate to get some sort of exemption from the EU’s “Made in Europe” procurement laws and Healey will be making the case for this to his European counterparts.
According to Treasury sources briefing overnight, Healey will be urging the EU to implement the “Made in Europe” rules in a way that “lands a good deal for all” instead of “erecting new barriers”.
Burnham is due to meet Martin at 10am.
Otherwise, the political diary is fairly empty.

articles.title: Australia: Man killed in shark attack near Perth
articles.summary: A swimmer was mauled by a shark, with witnesses reporting a massive pool of blood in the water. There have been four confirmed fatal shark attacks in Australia this year.

image.caption: Four people have been confirmed killed by sharks in Australia this year [FILE JUNE 2026]Image: Hollie Adams/REUTERS

blocks.text: A swimmer off the coast of Perth in Western Australia was killed by a shark on Friday, police said.

Emergency services were called to Sorrento Beach in the north of the city to search for the man. Earlier, witnesses said they had watched the man being attacked by a shark, with blood pooling in the water, Australian media reported.
It is unclear whether any remains were recovered, and no details of the victim's identity have yet been shared.
"It was reported a male swimmer had been bitten by a shark while swimming along the coast," a Western Australia state police spokeswoman said in a statement.
"The swimmer died as a result of the attack."
The beach was closed following the attack.
Several killed this year by sharks
Friday's incident would be the fifth fatal shark attack in Australia this year. Previously, there were four confirmed fatal shark attacks.
In May and June, three spearfishing divers were killed by sharks in seperate incidents. In January, a 12-year-old boy died in hospital after being mauled by a bull shark in Sydney Harbor.
On Monday, a surfer was severely wounded in the leg near the city of Geraldton, 400 kilometers (250 miles) north of Perth on Australia's west coast.
Over the past 25 years, Australia has averaged between two and three fatal shark attacks annually, according to the Australian Shark Incident Database.
